:::{#exm-npv}
#### NPV of a COVID-19 test

For the COVID-19 test of @exm-sensitivity and @exm-specificity,
used in the population of @exm-prevalence,
the probability of a negative test for a person with COVID-19 is,
by the
[complement rule](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#cor-p-neg0):

$$
\ba
\Pr(\neg + \mid D)
&= 1 - \Pr(+ \mid D)
&& \text{(complement rule, conditional on } D \text{)} \\
&= 1 - 0.99
&& \text{(substitute the sensitivity)} \\
&= 0.01
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

By
[Bayes' theorem](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#thm-bayes),
with the denominator expanded by the
[law of total probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#thm-total-prob)
over the partition $\set{D, \neg D}$,
the negative predictive value (@def-npv) is:

$$
\ba
\Pr(\neg D \mid \neg +)
&= \frac{\Pr(\neg + \mid \neg D) \cd \Pr(\neg D)}{\Pr(\neg +)}
&& \text{(Bayes' theorem)} \\
&= \frac{\Pr(\neg + \mid \neg D) \cd \Pr(\neg D)}{\Pr(\neg + \mid \neg D) \cd \Pr(\neg D) + \Pr(\neg + \mid D) \cd \Pr(D)}
&& \text{(law of total probability)} \\
&= \frac{0.99 \cd 0.93}{0.99 \cd 0.93 + 0.01 \cd 0.07}
&& \text{(substitute the given values)} \\
&= \frac{0.9207}{0.9207 + 0.0007}
&& \text{(multiply each term in the numerator and denominator)} \\
&= \frac{0.9207}{0.9214}
&& \text{(add the denominator's two terms)} \\
&\approx 0.9992
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

A negative result from this test is very reliable:
only about 8 in 10,000 people who test negative have COVID-19.

:::
